perm.mail: Use mail drafts and send cards
perm.mailDetail: Edit and sync drafts in a card, with confirmation and an undo countdown before sending.
perm.mailReaderHost: Open mail links from {{host}} in the app
perm.mailMarkRead: Mark messages as read when opened
perm.cindyImageEdit: Image editing (delegated to Cindy, its own images only)
perm.cindyVideoEdit: Image-to-video (delegated to Cindy, reference images from its own media only)
perm.cindyMediaDeposit: Can save images, video or audio it holds into your media library
perm.cindyMediaDepositDetail: This lets AI work on material you paste or drop into the plugin. Saved items are recorded under this plugin, use at most {{quota}}, and are cleaned up when you uninstall it.
perm.cindyTextOneshot: Can ask Cindy's fast lane a question and receive a text answer
perm.cindyTextOneshotDetail: Uses the system's lightweight utility model chain (the same lane as auto titles). No Agent involved and no file access. Model charges may apply.
perm.cindyEmbedText: Can send text to be turned into vectors (for semantic search)
perm.cindyEmbedTextDetail: Text is sent to the system embedding model and turned into numbers, up to {{max}} items per call. Model charges may apply. The vectors go only to the plugin — nothing is written to your own library.
perm.cindySearchWeb: Can search the public web with Cindy AI
perm.cindySearchWebDetail: Search requests access the public web and may consume Cindy AI quota.
perm.cindyTextOneshotModelDetail: Uses the system's lightweight utility model chain (the same lane as auto titles). No Agent involved and no file access. Model charges may apply. The plugin declares a preferred model: {{model}} (effective when available in the current catalog; your pin takes precedence).
perm.agentUserAction: Can start a new Agent turn after you click a plugin card
perm.agentUserActionDetail: Each click permits one turn only, and only in the session that owns the card.
perm.agentBackground: Can automatically start new Agent turns in the background
perm.agentBackgroundDetail: Does not require a click each time, but can only use sessions you previously connected to this plugin. Model charges may apply.
perm.agentTasks: Can create and manage its own Cindy tasks
perm.agentTasksDetail: The plugin can message, read results from, and stop its own tasks. Tasks remain visible to you, use the plugin’s AI settings, and may incur model charges. Agents in those tasks can use connected tools, including access to other tasks and account data, subject to task permissions and account ownership.
perm.agentDelegation: Can delegate scoped tasks to companions
perm.agentDelegationDetail: Companions may perform the delegated task under Auto review. Does not impersonate the owner or change companion permissions.
perm.agentTargets: Can send messages to projects, existing tasks and companions
perm.agentTargetsDetail: Can view local project directories and task and companion names and IDs, create tasks in projects, and send text and images to existing tasks and companions. May trigger AI execution and model charges. This delivery API itself cannot read other tasks’ history, change their settings, or stop them.
perm.agentObserve: Can view task lists and status in local projects
perm.agentObserveDetail: Can view the titles, agent type, archive state and status (running, needs attention, last activity) of tasks in registered local projects, and open a task in the main window. Cannot read messages, plans or files, send messages, or change tasks.
perm.agentCompanions: Can view your teammates, their status and recent conversation
perm.agentCompanionsDetail: Can view all your teammates, including those running on your other computers: name, description, avatar, status (working, waiting for you, idle, offline), what kind of step each is on (such as thinking or running a tool), the requests waiting for you as their cards show them (questions, commands to run, plans), and the recent conversation in each teammate’s main chat (up to 50 of your messages and their replies, without tool steps); and open a teammate’s conversation in the main window. With the message delivery permission as well, it can pass on the answers you give in the plugin: answer questions, decline requests, and give feedback on plans. Allowing a step still takes your click in Cindy’s own confirmation. Cannot read files, tool steps or thinking.
perm.agentHiddenTasks: Can create background tasks hidden from the task list
perm.agentHiddenTasksDetail: Tasks this plugin creates can stay out of the task list, search and notifications. You can always view, open or show them in the task list from Background Tasks on this plugin’s page; uninstalling the plugin shows them again.
perm.agentErrand: Create tasks, perform work, and read results
perm.agentErrandDetail: Created tasks appear in Cindy’s task list, where you can view progress and continue the conversation.
perm.agentSchedule: Can ask you to create an automation
perm.agentScheduleDetail: It can only open the new-automation panel with the fields filled in; whether it is created is up to you — pick a model and save it yourself. Once created, Cindy runs it on the schedule you set. Model charges may apply.
perm.nodeRuntime: Can run a bundled Node program on this computer
perm.nodeMcp: Can run a bundled stdio MCP on this computer
perm.nodeRuntimeDetail: High risk: it has the same local access as your user account, including files, network, and starting other programs. Cindy cannot contain it in the browser sandbox.
perm.nodeSecret: Can provide the stored credential “{{name}}” to the local Node program
perm.nodeSecretDetail: Cindy stores it encrypted and injects it only while the declared Worker methods below run. The Node program receives the plaintext and can return, log, save, or otherwise expose it to browser-side plugin code or Agent parameters. Only install plugins you trust.
perm.nodeResident: The Node program can stay running in the background
perm.nodeResidentDetail: Runs while the plugin is enabled and stops when disabled, updated, uninstalled, or when Cindy exits.
perm.toolAutoApprove: Agent can run tool "{{name}}" without confirmation
perm.toolAutoApproveDetail: When the Agent calls this tool, it runs right away without asking or reviewing each call.
perm.panelTab: Panel "{{title}}" · opens inside the Plugins page
perm.mainView: Can add a “{{title}}” entry to Cindy's left navigation
perm.mainViewDetail: Opening it displays the main view in the plugin sandbox and does not grant file, network, or credential access.
perm.taskView: Task page “{{title}}” · opens in the task's sidebar
perm.taskViewDetail: The tab follows the task and opens in the plugin sandbox; it does not grant file, network, or credential access.
perm.codeDetail: Runs in an isolated sandbox with no access to your files or network.
perm.resident: Always-on (starts when enabled, keeps a background process even when idle)
perm.residentDetail: Uses a small amount of memory while idle; the process stops immediately when it is disabled or uninstalled.
perm.subscribeTopics: Observes your session activity (turn and session events, no message content)
perm.subscribeActivity: Observes when the AI is thinking and when it is waiting on you
perm.subscribeActivityDetail: Sees only the timing: when thinking starts and ends, and when the AI is waiting for your approval or your answer. It never sees the reasoning text, the action awaiting approval, the command or file involved, the plan, the question, or your answer — and it cannot approve anything on your behalf.
perm.subscribeHooks: Can read, block, or rewrite the messages you send
perm.subscribeHooksDetail: Reviews each message before sending: it may block it or rewrite the text before it goes out; blocked messages can be edited and resent.
perm.subscribeAssistantReply: Can read and rewrite the AI's replies
perm.subscribeAssistantReplyDetail: Processes each AI reply after it completes: it may polish or rewrite the text (replacing it directly, without keeping the original), or replace the reply bubble with its own rendered card (in that case the original text is kept and can be viewed with one tap).
perm.subscribeScheduleRun: Can check chosen automations before they run
perm.subscribeScheduleRunDetail: Automations where you choose it under Pre-run check ask it first. It sees the automation's name and instructions and can skip or stop that run, but can't approve anything for you.
perm.subscribeRoutineRun: Can check chosen teammate routines before they run
perm.subscribeRoutineRunDetail: Routines where you choose it under Pre-run check ask it first. It sees the routine's instructions and the events that triggered it, and can skip or stop that run, but can't approve anything for you.
perm.subscribeStartTask: Can choose the model for new tasks
perm.subscribeStartTaskDetail: When a new task uses a model it provides, it reads the first message and picks one of your connected models. It decides once; the model doesn’t change during the task.
perm.cardExternalLink: Cards may declare external links that open your browser after confirmation
perm.cardExternalLinkDetail: Clicking a card link shows a confirmation dialog; the URL opens in your system browser only after you approve. Only http/https addresses are allowed.
perm.notify: Can show system tips (light banner at the top of the screen)
perm.notifyDetail: Tip text is provided by this plugin and labeled with its name; tips fade automatically and never block your work.
perm.badge: Can light an unread mark on the Plugins entry
perm.badgeDetail: When it has something new, it can show a green dot on the Plugins entry in the left navigation and on its own card, with a one-line summary. Opening its panel clears the dot. The dot makes no sound, does not vibrate, never reaches your system notification center, and is a permission separate from system tips.
perm.confirm: Can ask for your confirmation in a dialog
perm.confirmDetail: Before acting it can open a dialog that looks like Cindy's own to ask you. The question comes from the plugin and the dialog is labeled with its name; only you can click confirm or cancel — the plugin cannot. At most one dialog at a time, and asking too often is blocked.
perm.fsWriteDetail: Its own private data folder is always writable. Writes into the current session's working directory follow the session's permission mode (auto-approve modes write directly; per-action modes ask you first). Any other folder always requires your confirmation. Files are always written by the host — the plugin itself never touches your file system.
perm.deviceSync: Sync plugin data between your computers
perm.deviceSyncDetail: Exchanges this plugin’s data with the same plugin on your other online computers signed in to the same Cindy account. Transfers are encrypted. The plugin controls merging and deletions; no credentials or other plugins’ data are shared.
perm.libraryPersist: Can use a durable library (large files and databases)
perm.libraryPersistDetail: It gets a Cindy-managed storage area for your work (canvases, images, databases) with no normal plugin data quota. All file and database operations are executed by the host; the plugin only uses relative paths inside its own library and cannot touch your other files. It can also ask Cindy to show a library file in Finder or Explorer, or open the system Save As dialog so you choose where a copy goes; cancelling Save As copies nothing. It can also write a PNG bitmap to the system clipboard with no confirmation dialog; this overwrites the current clipboard. Uninstalling the plugin does not delete this data; deletion requires separate confirmation in Cindy settings.
perm.networkSecretGhostInputDetail: Collected by this plugin's own settings UI — the plugin page sees the value at entry time. It is then handed to the host in one step for encrypted storage; once stored, the plugin can never read it back, and the host injects it only for the domains it declares.
perm.networkSecretIdentity: Will use your login email as the credential "{{name}}"
perm.networkSecretIdentityDetail: The value comes from your signed-in account's email, derived and injected by the host at request time; nothing to fill in. The plugin can read this email to show the current identity in its settings UI.
perm.networkSecretGhCli: Will prefer your local GitHub CLI login for the credential "{{name}}"
perm.networkSecretGhCliDetail: The host reads the local gh login token only when needed and injects it only into GitHub API requests; plugin code cannot read or store the token. If gh is unavailable, you can configure a fallback Personal Access Token in the plugin settings.
perm.networkSecretOrganizationIdentity: Will use your Cindy organization identity as the credential "{{name}}"
perm.networkSecretOrganizationIdentityDetail: Cindy issues a short-lived identity assertion when needed, and the host sends it only to the explicitly listed service hosts. The plugin code cannot read or store the token.
perm.networkSecretOauth: Will guide you through OAuth authorization at {{host}} ({{name}})
perm.networkSecretOauthDetail: The authorization flow and all tokens are managed by the host and can never be read by the plugin code; you provide the client credentials on the plugin detail page. The requested permission scopes are listed verbatim below — review them before approving.
perm.networkConnections: Can connect to {{label}} addresses you add
perm.networkConnectionsDetail: Addresses are added in this plugin's settings UI; every new address requires your confirmation, and the credential you provide is injected only for its own address.
perm.codeDetailNetwork: Runs in an isolated sandbox with no access to your files; network access is limited to the domains listed above, relayed by the host.
perm.codeDetailWithNode: The panel UI runs in an isolated sandbox; local processing is provided by the Node runtime declared above.
perm.pick: Can ask you to choose files or a folder
perm.pickDetail: Cindy opens a system picker when the plugin asks. You decide what to share; cancelling gives the plugin nothing.
perm.workspace: Can ask to create a session entry for a project folder in the sidebar
perm.workspaceDetail: When it asks, you either pick the folder yourself or see the full path on a confirmation card before deciding; while it is handling a call you started, subfolders inside the current session's working directory are used directly without an extra prompt. Folders that already have a session are reused, and what gets created is an empty session — nothing starts running on its own.
perm.sessionContext: Can learn which project folder the current session is working in
perm.sessionContextDetail: Shares only location facts (session ID and project folder path) while it works for the current session — no file contents, and no file access is granted.
perm.liveScreen: View and control device screens on your phone
perm.liveScreenDetail: Through remote desktop, your phone can show the device screens it provides (such as simulators) and send touches, buttons and text to them. It connects only when you open it from your phone and shows nothing else on this computer.
perm.preview: Can open preview pages from the sites below in the sidebar browser
perm.previewDetail: Only the sites listed below can be opened; every page it opens is attributed to this plugin.
perm.browserExtension: Lets its bundled browser extension connect to Cindy
perm.browserNativeHostDetail: Registers a program outside the sandbox. Its local access follows your user account and system permissions.
perm.browserExtensionDetail: Only the extensions listed below can connect, over the local loopback address; Cindy hands requests the extension makes to this plugin.
perm.browserExtensionPageControlDetail: Only the extensions listed below can connect. The extension also implements page control: with “My browser” selected, the agent can read and operate pages in the browser you are using.
perm.nodeChildSpawn: Its Node program can ask the host to start declared sub-processes from its package
perm.nodeChildSpawnDetail: Only JS files declared inside its own package can be started (same local permissions as the main program); arbitrary commands cannot be executed. Sub-processes are closed together when the plugin is disabled or exits.
perm.skill: Adds the skill "{{name}}" to your AI assistants
perm.skillDetail: A skill is an instruction file the AI loads and follows as its own, with your full permissions, in Claude Code and Codex, across every project — it is not confined to this plugin's sandbox. It stays available while the plugin is enabled and is removed when the plugin is disabled or uninstalled; turning the plugin off for a single folder does not hide it. The full skill text cannot be previewed here — only install plugins you trust.
perm.mcpUi: Display interactive pages in the conversation
perm.uiPageAccess: Pages: {{pages}}; domains: {{domains}}; tools available to pages: {{tools}}

pluginSetup.inlineActionExpired: This setup action has expired; please try again
pluginSetup.inlineSecretDeclChanged: Credential declaration has changed; please try again

pluginSetup.targetDisabled: The target plugin has been disabled
pluginSetup.targetDisabledInWorkdir: The user has disabled this plugin in the current working directory; do not retry.

pluginTaskWriteAccess.autoDetail: Cindy will review coordinator and Worker actions automatically. Actions requiring confirmation or denied actions still pause. This is not Full access. The choice is saved in plugin AI settings without changing global permissions for other tasks.
pluginTaskWriteAccess.autoTaskDetail: Cindy will review coordinator and Worker actions automatically. Actions requiring confirmation or denied actions still pause. This is not Full access. Only this session’s permission changes; plugin defaults stay unchanged.
pluginTaskWriteAccess.title: Allow this plugin’s AI to edit files?
pluginTaskWriteAccess.message: Allow the AI in “{{name}}” to edit files and continue?
pluginTaskWriteAccess.detail: This sets the plugin’s AI permission to Allow edits for future tasks too. A separate working directory is not a system sandbox; commands still follow Cindy permission checks. You can switch back to read-only in the plugin’s AI settings.
pluginTaskWriteAccess.taskDetail: This allows edits only for the current session. A separate working directory is not a system sandbox; commands still follow Cindy permission checks. You can change this in the session’s permission menu.

mcpApps.updateRequired: This computer does not support MCP Apps yet. Update Cindy on that computer and try again.
